paraphrase: On a logic of attitudes built like Hare's phrastic/neustic model, where moral and non-moral judgments differ by attitude type, logical relations among judgments must be explained by inconsistency between attitude types (Schroeder's B-type), with new attitude types for complex sentences; Schroeder holds the clearest genuine inconsistencies to be A-type and so prefers an A-type model if one can be built. Scoped to that architecture: constant meaning alone entails neither cost.
